Dash-pot damper. The red weight, when positioned correctly, will act as a damper on the oscillation system. A "tuned damper" (<-keyword) will diminish the oscillation the fastest possible way. An "untuned damper" or one with the weight in the back, will cause a feedback loop in the oscillations and cause larger and larger wiggles until the whole trailer and car jackknife.

Simply put, the weight induces a moment (or torque) on the trailer. When the weight is close to the car the moment arm is shorter so there is less torque.

When it is farther away the moment arm is longer so there is more torque.

Torque is the force multiplied by the distance which is why it is expressed in units of lbft or Nm.
